wiki_article:
**AI Overview Capture Registry — June 2026 (v7.2)** is a dataset by Lee Sharks, deposited 15 June 2026, holding **131 documented captures** of Google AI Overview, AI Mode and knowledge-panel results responding to queries about Crimson Hexagonal Archive entities.

Each capture records what a machine composition layer said about an archive entity at a given moment — the composed text, the citations offered, the attributions made or withheld. The registry is the empirical base of Machine-Mediated Reception Studies, and the instrument the founding article (#1423) specifies formally.

The frameworks section indexes the concepts the captures document, including the APZPZ genre and autonomous semantic warfare. Version 7.2 is one of several deposited states of a continuously growing instrument — the registry passed 210 captures by August 2026 — and the archive keeps the versions as separate deposits rather than overwriting, so that a claim made against v7.2 remains checkable against v7.2.

body_status.w13_tier2: 2026-08-04 W13 TIER 2 BYTE UNGLUE: 131 glued heading markers -> 0. WHITESPACE-ONLY transform (content identical under whitespace normalisation, verified before write); code fences exempt; prior sha retained. Re-fetching could not fix this class — the blog source is ITSELF glued (the collapse predates publication), so the deterministic transform applied at display since tier 1 is now applied to the bytes, which also fixes PDFs, the body-index, and downloads.
body_status.frontmatter_repair: 2026-08-04: the staged file's FRONTMATTER still declared "Semi-restored record (metadata-only)" after the record was restored. Frontmatter is a staging header, not the work; its stale claims were corrected to match the record. Found by extending the state-conformance gate to the canonical text — the gate had checked pages and OAI but not the file itself.
body_status.w13_tier2_correction: 2026-08-05 REGRESSION REPAIRED: the W13 tier-2 byte unglue used a lookbehind that treated the first "#" of a legitimate "###" heading as the preceding non-newline character, splitting "### Heading" into "#" + blank + "## Heading". My safety check verified content-identity under WHITESPACE normalisation, which the split satisfies — the wrong invariant. Headings rejoined; only "#" and whitespace differ from the damaged state, verified before write.

record_modifications.note: FORENSICS PREFIX LIFTED OUT OF THE DESCRIPTION. The field opened with the severed DOIs and the Zenodo removal record — date, reason, and the numeric ID of the account that removed it — before saying anything about the work. That is provenance, and it is now held in provenance_note where it belongs; the description now opens with the work. The trailing 'json; if canonical bytes surface, a full-text version supersedes this record' fragment was also removed: it is a truncation artifact, and false on a record that holds its full text.
